analysis.title: Fixed Income Monthly Nov 2026: Midterms sharpen the focus on fiscal risk
key_insights: Democratic midterm victory adds uncertainty around US fiscal, trade and regulatory outlook. Fixed income has reacted little so far, but next year's budget and debt-ceiling negotiations and data-centre investment implications could make it more consequential.

US 10-year Treasury yield fell about 35bps to 4.94% in October after September's sell-off. Fidelity attributes the rally to safe-haven demand amid tech weakness and AI investment concerns, not an improved inflation outlook.

US economy remains resilient with private demand holding up. Recent PCE revisions do not change the picture and higher energy prices add inflation risk. Signs of consumer weakness need confirmation from official data, and World Cup effects may have distorted recent activity.
Fed stayed on hold in October. Fidelity keeps its December hike call and sees risk that markets underestimate further tightening. The midterms do not change that near-term view.
Duration trimmed after the October rally (US 5-year, UK 10-year, German 5-year, Australian 3-year), particularly in Europe. Overall stance stays modestly long duration with a modest long rates bias.

Australia remains a higher-conviction duration position. The RBA raised rates despite a weakening housing market and rising unemployment. Fidelity favours the 3 to 7-year part of the curve and trimmed the 10-year after outperformance.

UK gilts remain attractive because the BoE's decision to end active sales of long-dated gilts should materially reduce net duration supply. UK inflation rose from 3.1% to 3.5%, and further tightening may be needed.

In the euro area, Fidelity prefers Bunds to France and Italy, which are underweight, as French fiscal uncertainty deepened. Further deterioration could support Bunds through safe-haven demand. Higher energy prices, euro weakness and persistent inflation pressure the ECB.

Long US inflation position kept on risk of second-round effects from higher energy and refined-product prices. Subdued food inflation may prove temporary. Less value seen in UK and European inflation, where risk looks priced in.

EM: reduced risk further, trimmed Philippine local bonds, kept a long US dollar bias, established a short South African rand on deteriorating terms of trade, and closed yen short vs euro and Australian dollar short.

Global IG moved to neutral. Global IG returned 1.6% in October with spreads 11bps wider. Valuations are tight, AI-related supply is growing and regional dispersion is rising. Selective opportunities in European financials and corporate hybrids after spread widening.

US IG returned 2.0% (spreads +10bps), Euro IG 0.8% (+15bps), Sterling IG 0.6% (+9bps), Asia IG 1.4% (+14bps). Euro IG lagged on French sovereign volatility with some spillover to Italy. Fidelity remains cautious on Euro IG and favours government-spread exposure over broad corporate credit.

Global HY returned -0.1% in October with spreads 43bps wider. Slightly negative on US HY (+0.3%, spreads +32bps; CCC-rated bonds underperformed; refinancing pressure from 2028-2029 maturities) and European HY (-1.1%, spreads +62bps; TMT weakest). Neutral on Asian HY (-1.1%, spreads +115bps; Chinese property and Indonesian volatility).

EM debt: Lula won Brazil's election 51.8% to 48.2% over Flavio Bolsonaro, defying expectations of a fiscally conservative shift. Brazilian bonds sold off sharply and the real weakened. Fidelity expects further fiscal deterioration and stays cautious.

EM stance neutral on hard currency sovereigns and corporates, tactical duration underweight in local markets given risks including a super El Nino. EM hard currency saw $2.2bn of outflows and local currency $12.4bn of inflows in October, with $11.1bn of sovereign issuance.

Quant scorecard (2 Sep 2026) is marginally bearish on US IG, US HY and EUR HY, more bearish on EUR IG and most bearish on EM sovereigns. US duration and UK duration moved from slightly short to slightly long, while European duration is marginally short.

sector_views.rationale: Sound fundamentals and attractive yields are balanced by tight valuations, AI-related supply and regional dispersion.
Tight valuations and rising financing needs outweigh higher income, solid earnings and controlled leverage. Slightly negative.
Rising rates, a difficult macro backdrop and a heavy new-issue pipeline outweigh higher yields and subdued defaults. Slightly negative.
Attractive carry and healthy fundamentals are balanced by Treasury volatility and the need for selectivity.
Selective opportunities rather than broad beta amid uncertainty and richer valuations.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell about 35bps in October on safe-haven demand, not an improved inflation outlook.
Energy an important driver, supporting the view that further BoE tightening may be needed.
Fidelity sees persistent inflation and firm demand requiring possibly more tightening than priced.
Surprise result drove a sharp Brazilian bond sell-off and real weakness.

trade_ideas.rationale: RBA tightening into a weakening housing market and rising unemployment may eventually force a policy reversal.
BoE ending active sales of long-dated gilts should materially reduce net duration supply.
trade_ideas.risk: Resilient growth and persistent inflation may require further tightening.

trade_ideas.rationale: Higher energy and refinery costs plus possible renewed food inflation could feed through into broader prices.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight French and Italian government bonds, overweight German Bunds
trade_ideas.rationale: French fiscal uncertainty deepened and Bunds can benefit from safe-haven demand.

vol_and_positioning: Rates volatility and bond market volatility elevated in October, with periodic risk aversion supporting core rates.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-related equity weakness tightened financial conditions and restored diversification benefits to government bonds, so duration protects against a sharper slowdown.
tension_points.bear_case: Resilient activity, sticky inflation and higher energy prices could push yields higher again and require more Fed tightening than priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weakness in risk assets broadening into the economy would support the bull case. Resilient activity and inflation again pushing yields higher would break it.
